guards.compilation: AST-only compile allowed; executable compile only exact local archive reader bytes
guards.execution: all exec/eval denied except byte-identical compiled hash-pinned local archive_reader.py
guards.extraction: ZIP/TAR filesystem extraction and shutil.unpack_archive denied
guards.loading: new imports, extension loading and ctypes shared library loading denied
guards.network: socket construction/name resolution and socket audit events denied
guards.open: CPython audit open event: exact files, read only, verified descriptor identities
guards.process: subprocess, os.system/popen/exec/spawn/fork and audit events denied
guards.writes: write-mode opens, mutation, enumeration, mmap and process audit events denied

limits: One pinned FP16 original only; no BF16 or fresh c6 guarded run is claimed.
Python runtime audit/hooks plus static source inventory are not an OS sandbox or proof against a hostile interpreter.
Trusted standard-library and local reader modules are imported before guards; their startup imports are outside this dynamic boundary.
The public loader's exact trusted local archive_reader.py is repeatedly source-verified and allowed to execute; this is not retained payload execution.
Denied local bytecode-cache reads force the unmodified loader to fall back to pinned source; those denials are separately classified.
Native execution, acceptance, arbitrary-origin authentication, missing third-party bytes and full supplementary host-fault semantics remain unclaimed.

limitations: Replay checks retained consistency; it does not authenticate an arbitrary producer or execute a GPU.
The selected archive digest and execution revision must come from independently retained intake evidence.
Recorded runner paths are lexical data; archived code, binaries and wheels are never executed or extracted.
Third-party wheel and installed payload bytes, interpreter/seed bytes and venv configuration contents are not fully retained.
Their recorded identities and inventories can be reconciled, but missing bytes cannot be freshly hashed by replay.
One format is not the complete two-format qualification; copied packets add no executions.
Host fault-test reports remain host evidence. This reader does not grant framework, performance or phase acceptance.
Supplementary preparation and host fault packets have bounded envelope and byte-identity checks only; their fault, build and preparation semantics are not revalidated.
